name_zh: 普古里茶园大吉岭红茶
processing: Organic Darjeeling, known for clonal tea. Orthodox rolling and firing is typical of the district, with oxidation depending on the flush.
harvest_season: Not recorded in detail for this garden. As across Darjeeling, spring and summer flushes are the best-known pickings.
appearance_dry: Typically twisted olive to brown leaf with some pale tips, as clonal Darjeelings often show.
appearance_wet: Mixed green and copper leaf, greener in spring lots.
taste_profile: Little is recorded about this garden's cup. Clonal Darjeelings typically lean aromatic and floral, with more fruit in the summer pick.

brewing.notes: Western-style brew; clonal lots can sharpen in very hot water, so start cooler and adjust.

vintage_note: Sold by year and flush, usually as current-season organic lots. Spring teas are best within about a year, as is usual for first flush Darjeeling.
description:
Phuguri is an organic Darjeeling garden 7 km from Mirik, planted on about 433 hectares between roughly 1,100 and 1,800 metres. It is best known for clonal tea, grown from selected bushes rather than from seed.

That clonal focus matters in the cup, since such bushes are generally chosen for aroma. The garden's output is around 150,000 kg of organic tea a year, and it holds several organic and fair-trade certifications.

Specific tasting notes for it are hard to pin down. Typical of clonal Darjeeling, look for an aromatic, floral spring cup and a rounder summer one. Start with cooler water and short steeps.

When buying, check for the flush and year. Organic certification is the garden's selling point, and it should be stated on the lot.
history: The land was a freehold grant to Dakman Rai, a Nepali nobleman who brought settlers to Darjeeling at Dr Campbell's request. He also received what became Soureni and Samripani. The Phuguri estate itself was set up in 1880 and now belongs to the Bagaria Group.
